title.zh: 卷九十 列傳第五十 明四王
title.raw: 卷九十 列傳第五十 明四王 Volume 90 Biographies 50: Ming Siwang

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十 明四王

translations.literal: Biography 50: The Four Princes of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 50: the four sons of Emperor Ming who received princely rank.

sentences.zh: 明帝十二子：陳貴妃生後廢帝，謝脩儀生皇子法良，陳昭華生順帝，徐婕妤生第四皇子，鄭脩容生皇子智井，次晉熙王燮，與皇子法良同生。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming had twelve sons: Honored Consort Chen bore the later deposed emperor; Lady Xie Xiuyi bore Prince Fa-liang; Lady Chen Zhaohua bore Emperor Shun; Lady Xu Jieyu bore the Fourth Prince; Lady Zheng Xiurong bore Prince Zhijing; next Prince Xie of Jinxi, born of the same mother as Prince Fa-liang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming fathered twelve sons: Consort Chen’s son became the later deposed ruler; Lady Xie’s son was Prince Fa-liang; Lady Chen the Bright Consort bore Shun; Lady Xu the Fourth Prince; Lady Zheng bore Prince Zhijing; next came Prince Xie of Jinxi, Fa-liang’s full brother.

translations.literal: Lady Quan the Meiren bore Prince You, posthumously titled Prince Shao-ling;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Quan gave birth to Prince You, posthumously ennobled as Prince Shao-ling.

sentences.zh: 次江夏王躋，與第四皇子同生。

translations.literal: Next Prince Ji of Jiangxia, born of the same mother as the Fourth Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Next was Prince Ji of Jiangxia, the Fourth Prince’s full brother.

sentences.zh: 徐良人生武陵王贊，杜脩華生隨陽王翽。

translations.literal: Lady Xu the Liangren bore Prince Zan of Wuling; Lady Du Xiuhua bore Prince Hui of Suiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xu of lower rank bore Prince Zan of Wuling; Lady Du the Accomplished bore Prince Hui of Suiyang.

sentences.zh: 次新興王嵩，與武陵王贊同生。

translations.literal: Next Prince Song of Xinxing, born of the same mother as Prince Zan of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: Then came Prince Song of Xinxing, Prince Zan’s twin by the same mother.

translations.literal: Again Lady Quan the Meiren bore Prince Xi of Shijian.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Quan also bore Prince Xi of Shijian.

translations.literal: Zhi-jing, Xie, Ji, and Zan all went out to continue other lines.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijing, Xie, Ji, and Zan were each given in adoption to continue collateral houses.

sentences.zh: 法良未封，第四皇子未有名，早夭。

translations.literal: Fa-liang received no fief; the Fourth Prince never received a name; both died young.
translations.idiomatic: Fa-liang died before investiture; the Fourth Prince never even received a personal name—both perished in childhood.

sentences.zh: 新興王嵩，字仲嶽，明帝第十一子。

translations.literal: Prince Song of Xinxing, courtesy name Zhongyue, was Emperor Ming’s eleventh son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Song of Xinxing, styled Zhongyue, was the eleventh son of Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 元徽四年，年六歲，封新興王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhui, age six, he was enfeoffed Prince of Xinxing, with revenue from two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In 476, at the age of six, he was made Prince of Xinxing with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，降封定襄縣公，食邑千五百戶。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was demoted to Duke of Dingxiang County, with revenue from one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi founder took the throne from the Song, Song was reduced to county duke of Dingxiang with fifteen hundred households.

translations.literal: He plotted rebellion and was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of plotting rebellion, he was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 始建王禧，字仲安，明帝第十二子也。

translations.literal: Prince Xi of Shijian, courtesy name Zhongan, was Emperor Ming’s twelfth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi of Shijian, styled Zhongan, was the twelfth son of Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 元徽四年，年六歲，封始建王，食邑二千戶。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhui, age six, he was enfeoffed Prince of Shijian, with revenue from two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In 476, at the age of six, he was made Prince of Shijian with a fief of two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，降封荔封縣公，食邑千五百戶。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was demoted to Duke of Lifeng County, with revenue from one thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi succeeded the Song, Xi was demoted to county duke of Lifeng with fifteen hundred households.

translations.literal: He plotted rebellion and was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of plotting rebellion, he was ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：太宗負螟之慶，事非己出，枝葉不茂，豈能庇其本根。

translations.literal: The historians say: Taizong bore the blessing of the adopted heir; the matter was not born of himself; branches and leaves were not lush, and so could not shelter the root.
translations.idiomatic: The historians observed that Mingdi’s line rested on an adopted succession: those sons were not truly of his own issue, and a sparse canopy of twigs cannot shield the trunk.

translations.literal: To be enfeoffed as a lord under the Zhou—this was fortune enough.
translations.idiomatic: To end merely as a Zhou-style fief-holder was, under the circumstances, the kinder fate.
